'''''The Politics of Modelling, Numbers Between Science and Policy''''' is a multi-authors book edited by [[Andrea Saltelli]] and Monica Di Fiore and published in August 2023 by [[Oxford University Press]].

== Synopsis== 
The Politics of Modelling elaborates and expands on themes of responsible modelling from a manifesto published in the journal [[Nature (journal) | Nature ]] in 2020.<ref name="manifesto">{{cite journal |last1=Saltelli |first1=Andrea |display-authors=etal |title=Five ways to ensure that models serve society: a manifesto |journal=Nature |date=June 2020 |volume=582 |issue=7813 |pages=482–484 |doi=10.1038/d41586-020-01812-9 |pmid=32581374 |bibcode=2020Natur.582..482S |hdl=1885/219031 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> The text is structured into three main sections: ''Meeting Models'', ''The Rules'', and ''The Rules in Practice''.<ref name="Nabavi" >{{cite journal | vauthors=((Nabavi, E.)), ((Razavi, S.)) | journal=Science | title=The responsibility turnThe Politics of Modelling: Numbers Between Science and Policy Andrea Saltelli and Monica Di Fiore, Eds. Oxford University Press, 2023. 272 pp | volume=382 | issue=6672 | page=775 | date=17 November 2023 | issn=1095-9203 | doi=10.1126/science.adl3473| pmid=37972171 | s2cid=265221551 }}</ref><ref name="Melsen">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Melsen, L. A.)) | journal=Minerva | title=The Politics Behind Overinterpreted and Underexplored Models: A Review of Andrea Saltelli and Monica Di Fiore (eds.), The Politics of Modelling – Numbers between Science and Policy | date=17 February 2024 | volume=62 | pages=141–144 | issn=1573-1871 | doi=10.1007/s11024-024-09524-4 | s2cid=267700922 }}</ref> The combination of theory with policy relevant examples makes the book accessible to modellers, researchers of modelling, and policy makers.<ref name="Melsen"/>

The volume comes with a foreword of [[Wendy Nelson Espeland]] and a preface of [[Daniel Sarewitz]], with chapters from [[Andy Stirling]], [[Wolfgang Drechsler]], [[Philip B. Stark]], [[Ting Xu]], [[Paolo Vineis]], [[Andrea Saltelli]], and other scholars.

==Reception== 
The book argues that models live in a "state of exception" provided by their access to a wealth of methodology of analysis, and by their epistemic authority borrowed from mathematics. This state allows models to better defend an appearance of neutrality that is appreciated by policymakers in search of a justification.<ref>{{Citation | vauthors=((Tarran, B.)) | year=2023 | title='I would like modellers to be less ambitious in developing monster models that are impossible to inspect' | url=https://realworlddatascience.net/viewpoints/interviews/posts/2023/11/24/politics-of-modelling.html | access-date=25 November 2023}}</ref> A review published in the ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' notes that the volume incorporated insights from [[science and technology studies]] to explore modeling beyond its technical aspects<ref name="Nabavi" /> A second review<ref name="Melsen"/> in the ''[[Minerva (Springer journal)| Minerva]]'' notes the book's reference to the works of historians Margaret Morrison and [[Mary S. Morgan]] in considering [[Models as Mediators: Perspectives on Natural and Social Science |  models as mediators]] whereby models are simultaneously a tool, an interpretation, and a representation of the system.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Saltelli | first1=A. | last2=Di Fiore | first2=M. | editor-first1=Andrea | editor-first2=Monica | editor-last1=Saltelli | editor-last2=Di Fiore | year=2023 | title=The politics of modelling. Numbers between science and policy | publisher=Oxford University Press | location=Oxford | doi=10.1093/oso/9780198872412.001.0001 | isbn=978-0-19-887241-2 | url=https://academic.oup.com/book/46867?searchresult=1 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{rp|205}}
 
The book contrasts the danger of cynicism with suggestions to make models serve society, based on theory, examples, and a call for participatory modelling linked to [[Post-normal science]], [[sensitivity auditing]] and the concept of [[extended peer community]].<ref name="Melsen"/> Reviewers also noted<ref name="Melsen"/> that the book ignores other ongoing efforts in enhancing or formalizing modelling practices such as the framework proposed van Voorn,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Voorn, G. A. K. van)), ((Verburg, R. W.)), ((Kunseler, E.-M.)), ((Vader, J.)), ((Janssen, P. H. M.)) | journal=Environmental Modelling & Software | title=A checklist for model credibility, salience, and legitimacy to improve information transfer in environmental policy assessments | volume=83 | pages=224–236 | date=1 September 2016 | issn=1364-8152 | doi=10.1016/j.envsoft.2016.06.003| bibcode=2016EnvMS..83..224V | hdl=1874/334178 | s2cid=8363664 | hdl-access=free }}</ref> and the Good Modelling Practice handbook developed for water management purposes in the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite book | vauthors=((Waveren, H.)), ((Groot, S.)), ((Scholten, H.)), ((Geer, F.)), ((Wösten, H.)), ((Koeze, R.)), ((Noort, J.)) | date=1 January 1999 | title=Good Modelling Practice Handbook | publisher=STOWA | isbn=978-90-5773-056-6}}</ref>  Reviewers pointed to the book's failure to cover the 'fit-for purpose'<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Hamilton, S. H.)), ((Pollino, C. A.)), ((Stratford, D. S.)), ((Fu, B.)), ((Jakeman, A. J.)) | journal=Environmental Modelling & Software | title=Fit-for-purpose environmental modeling: Targeting the intersection of usability, reliability and feasibility | volume=148 | article-number=105278 | date=1 February 2022 | issn=1364-8152 | doi=10.1016/j.envsoft.2021.105278| bibcode=2022EnvMS.14805278H | s2cid=245155761 }}</ref> movement in modelling.<ref name="Nabavi"/> Other points where the book was found to be lacking by critics were the challenge of participatory modelling, related to gaming and power relations such as [[Public participation (decision making) | Arnsteinds' ladder of participation]].<ref name="Melsen"/>

A review in ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]''<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Campbell, P. J.)) | journal=Mathematics Magazine | title=Reviews: Saltelli, Andrea, and Monica Di Fiore (eds.), The Politics of Modelling: Numbers Between Science and Policy, Oxford University Press | volume=97 | issue=2 | pages=234–235 | publisher=Taylor & Francis | date=14 March 2024 | issn=0025-570X | doi=10.1080/0025570X.2024.2313390}}</ref> notes the book's attention to [[sensitivity analysis]]: "[The authors] stress the importance of sensitivity analysis, with a highly-illustrative and illuminating example that analyzes the EOQ (economic order quantity) formula." Another review<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Griffen, Z. W.)) | journal=Acta Sociologica | title=Book Review: The Politics of Modelling: Numbers Between Science and Policy by Andrea Saltelli and Monica Di Fiore | article-number=00016993251344539 | publisher=SAGE Publications Ltd | date=21 May 2025 | issn=0001-6993 | doi=10.1177/00016993251344539}}</ref>  in the journal [[Acta Sociologica]] notes that ''the collection brings the reflexive sensibility of social criticism to realworld applications: the pandemic, certainly, but also other arenas in which modeling serves as a technology of governance such as economics and climate change.''
